findings.title: Internal counts reconcile (Table 1 and Results, paragraphs 1-2)
findings.description: Every count in the paper reconciles exactly, with tolerance set to zero because these are counts that must hold exactly. findings.title: Null conclusion with no interval (Abstract, Conclusion; Discussion, final paragraph)
findings.description: THE CHECK COULD NOT RUN, AND THAT IS THE FINDING. absence_of_evidence requires an interval (or a coefficient with its standard error) to report the largest effect a null result still permits; this paper prints no confidence interval, no risk difference, no relative risk and no odds ratio anywhere -- for any quantity. The only effect estimate available is one this sweep derived from the Table 1 counts (Fisher odds ratio 1.56, from recalc_chi_squared), and it comes with no interval. With 5 events in 56 patients, 'not significant' here is very weak evidence of 'no difference', and the paper offers the reader no means of telling the two apart. No smallest effect size of interest is stated either

findings.title: Power analysis unverifiable (Discussion, paragraph 5)
findings.description: A RECORDED GAP IN THE TOOLKIT, not a defect in the paper. Every input needed is stated -- alpha 0.05, power 0.80 (written as beta = 0.20, the conventional type-II error notation), p1 = 0.05, p2 = 0.35, n = 28 per arm -- so the calculation is in principle fully reproducible. It could not be run because verify_power_analysis and required_n both take Cohen's h for a two-proportions design, and no registered tool derives h from two proportions. Two reporting observations that need no tool: the power calculation appears in the Discussion rather than the Methods, and the paper cites no trial registration or protocol, so it cannot be established that the calculation preceded data collection.

findings.description: Stated by quotation rather than computed, so no arithmetic is claimed here. The paper's own printed design parameters target a difference between a 5% and a 35% infection rate -- a 30-percentage-point gap. The observed result was 3 infections of 28 against 2 of 28, a one-patient difference. A trial sized for so large an effect cannot distinguish 'no difference' from 'a difference too small for this design to see', which is the substantive limitation on the paper's conclusion. The authors do note that 'the number was small' and call for larger studies, so the limitation is partly acknowledged; what is not acknowledged is that the Abstract states the conclusion without that qualification. findings.title: Table1 recovered from pdf
findings.description: The XML carries Table 1 as an image with no cells, so the paper's only table would have gone entirely unchecked from that source. The PDF extraction recovered the full 5-row grid (docling strategy, a read grid rather than text-alignment inference), and every number in it is independently corroborated by the Results prose, which restates the two age means with SDs and both infection counts. Because the two sources agree, the grid was treated as sound and used for the chi-squared and summation checks. No table in this paper is left unchecked for want of a source.
